newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto party workers clash with Karachi police.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto party workers clash with Karachi police.

text.p: About 5,000 supporters of Pakistan's deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto clashed with police as they welcomed her to Karachi on Saturday.

Pro-Bhutto demonstrators danced, waved flags of her Pakistan People's Party (PPP) and shouted slogans against President Farooq Leghari, who sacked Bhutto's government on November 5, saying it had been paralysed by corruption and misrule.
"Leghari is the killer of democracy," they chanted.
PPP leaders asked party workers to stay calm after they smashed signs and scuffled with police at Karachi airport. The trouble was minor and there were no reports of injuries.
Police in riot gear were out in force at the airport and along the route to Bilawal House, Bhutto's home in Karachi.
"You cannot strengthen democracy by breaking assemblies. At least one assembly should be given a chance to complete its term," Bhutto told her supporters at the airport.

Pakistani presidents have used controversial powers, inserted in the constitution by former military ruler General Mohammed Zia-ul-Haq in 1985, to dismiss four parliaments and four governments in the last eight years.
"I wonder why Leghari did this," Bhutto said. "I was happier when he got elected as president than at my own victory."
The PPP show of support for Bhutto was on a smaller scale than when she returned from exile in 1986 to challenge Zia.
"Our workers have come from all the five districts of Karachi. Some have come from far-flung villages. She (Bhutto) is the leader of the masses," one local PPP leader said.
"She will fight back and we will fight for her," said a woman demonstrator.

Witnesses said that supporters of the breakaway PPP-Shaheed Bhutto faction founded by Bhutto's slain brother Murtaza threw stones at PPP workers on their way to the airport, smashing the windows of at least half a dozen vehicles.
Murtaza Bhutto, a political rival of his sister, was shot dead by Karachi police in disputed circumstances on September 20. Bhutto has termed the killing a conspiracy against her.
